title: The peace prayer, honestly
hook: the prayer that asks to be made an instrument of peace wasn't written by Francis, though it's Franciscan in spirit

segments.voice: Yesterday, the patron of ecology, and a song that calls the sun brother and the earth sister and mother. Your line was brother earth. What did you call by a family name? Day one thousand two hundred twenty-five.

It's on the fridge magnet. It's on the framed print in the parish hall, under a picture of a friar with a bird on his hand. It gets read at weddings and funerals and sung at school Masses. It begins by asking God to make the one who prays an instrument of peace. And it often carries a name at the bottom: Saint Francis. Here's the honest part, and it's the whole lesson today. Francis didn't write it. So why does it carry his name, and does that change what it's worth?
screen: `ON THE FRIDGE, AT THE WEDDING.` → `SIGNED: SAINT FRANCIS.` → `HE DIDN'T WRITE IT.`

segments.voice: First, the prayer itself, in plain words. It asks to be made an instrument of peace. Then it walks through pairs: where there is hatred, let me bring love; where there is injury, pardon; doubt, faith; despair, hope; darkness, light; sadness, joy. Then it turns around. It asks to seek less to be comforted than to comfort, less to be understood than to understand, less to be loved than to love. And it ends with a run of reversals: in giving we receive, in pardoning we are pardoned, in dying we are born to eternal life. Now the history, as historians who traced it tell it. The prayer turns up long after Francis, in French, in a small church magazine, with no author's name at all. Later it was printed on a card with a picture of Francis, and the name traveled with the picture. No one seems to have meant to deceive. A prayer just found a face. So is it a fake? Not quite. It isn't by Francis, but it is shaped like him. Francis told his brothers, in his Testament, that God had shown him a greeting: the Lord give you peace. He walked into a war camp to meet a sultan. And the prayer's reversals, giving to receive, dying to live, sound like the man who said bitter became sweet. Jesus says it in the Beatitudes, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God." The honest way to pray it, then, is with both hands open: not his words, but his shape.
screen: `AN INSTRUMENT OF PEACE, IN PAIRS.` · `FIRST FOUND IN FRENCH, UNSIGNED.` · `A PRAYER THAT FOUND A FACE.` · `NOT HIS WORDS, BUT HIS SHAPE.` · then, large: `BLESSED ARE THE PEACEMAKERS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray it anyway, honestly. Settle, and breathe. If you know the peace prayer, pray it slowly, all the way through, knowing it comes from an unnamed hand and not from Assisi. If you don't know it, take just one pair. Bring to mind one place in your life where there is hatred, or injury, or sadness. Hold it for a few breaths. Then hold beside it the word the prayer pairs with it: love, or pardon, or joy. If you pray, you can offer that pair to God. If you don't, just let the two words sit side by side. The bell holds the time.
The peace prayer. A prayer to be made an instrument of peace, not written by Francis, but carrying his shape and his greeting. Today's word.

Your line: francis-shaped. It closes a week of lines: this one, christ first, seven joys, the custody, the hooded friars and brother earth. Today, do one thing that's Francis-shaped, even if no one will ever put his name on it. Day one thousand two hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Catholics and other Christians pray the peace prayer at home, in schools, and at weddings, funerals and public gatherings; Franciscans greet one another with words of peace drawn from Francis's Testament.

fork.setup: you learn that a prayer you love, signed with a saint's name, wasn't written by that saint. what do you do?
options: stop praying it: it's a fake.
pray it anyway, knowing whose shape it carries.
keep telling people the saint wrote it.
fork.reveal: it's unsigned and Francis-shaped, not his words, so the honest way is to pray it knowing both.

original.note: Latin: peace, the word at the heart of Francis's greeting and of the prayer that borrowed his name.

trapdoor: what you thought: Saint Francis wrote the peace prayer.
what it means: an unsigned prayer from long after him that sounds like him: peace, pardon, giving to receive.
what a scholar hears: the usual account is that it first appeared in a French church magazine and took Francis's name when it was printed on a card bearing his picture.

notes: Claims rule: the index hook's date ('around 1912': La Clochette, 1912, anonymous, 'Belle prière à faire pendant la messe') is not stated in the voice; the voice says 'long after Francis, in French, in a small church magazine, with no author's name'. The holy-card account (a card with Francis's image, c. 1920s) is given as 'as historians who traced it tell it' / 'the usual account'. Confirm.
The prayer is paraphrased, not quoted: its common English versions may not be public domain. Confirm the paraphrase of the pairs and the closing reversals.
The hook field is reworded from the index hook to avoid the date and to avoid quoting the English prayer; the index's 'lord, make me an instrument' is described instead.
'He walked into a war camp to meet a sultan' (Francis and al-Malik al-Kamil at Damietta) and 'bitter became sweet' (Testament; day 1208) are referenced briefly. Confirm.
